fluorescein leakage, subretinal fluid, and retinal leukocyte infiltration were established as in vivo imaging inflammatory markers in laser-induced CNVmice, and that anti-VEGF reduced retinal inflammation in this model.

leukocyte infiltration was established in a laser-induced choroidal neovascularization rodent model as an in vivo inflammatory marker and along showed response to anti-Vascular Endothelial Growth Factor therapy.

leukocytes labeled with 0.1% sodium fluorescin can be injected into the vitreous cavity of mice and can be used to visualize retinal inflammation in vivo in a laser-induced choroidal neovascularization model.

the use of sodium fluorescein as a leukocyte tracer for the in vivo imaging of retinal vascular inflammation.
